metadata.title: Compressing Neural Language Models by Sparse Word Representations

extraction_notes.note: Table 1 (parameter counts per subnet) and the perplexity/memory tables are floats, not text; their content is cited by the claims ClP1, ClP6-ClP11 rather than extracted as nodes.
The 'tricks' paragraph is a modification of the sparse-coding solver; extracted as an unmarked algorithm with three steps, the reformulated objective inside it as a problem.
theorem or claim: a cited NCE self-normalization result stated loosely in one sentence; typed theorem/external because it is a cited prior result.
Introduction contributions and the Conclusion restate later content; dataset description (4.1) and optimizer/threshold settings (4.2, 4.3.1) are experimental details, left out.
The ZRegression definition includes the following 'Hence' sentence giving the resulting probability (an unnumbered display), rather than a separate node.

nodes.statement: Although setting Z_h to 1 generally works well in our experiment, we find that in certain scenarios, the model is unstable. Experiments show that when the true normalization factor is far away from 1, the cost function may vibrate. To comply with NCE in general, we therefore propose a ZRegression layer to predict the normalization constant Z_h dependent on h, instead of treating it as a constant.
nodes.raw_latex:
Although setting $Z_h$ to 1 generally works well in our experiment, we find that in certain scenarios, the model is unstable. Experiments show that when the true normalization factor is far away from 1, the cost function may vibrate. To comply with NCE in general,
we therefore propose a \texttt{ZRegression} layer to predict the normalization constant $Z_h$ dependent on $h$, instead of treating it as a constant.
nodes.clean_text: Although setting Z_h to 1 generally works well in our experiment, we find that in certain scenarios, the model is unstable. Experiments show that when the true normalization factor is far away from 1, the cost function may vibrate. To comply with NCE in general, we therefore propose a ZRegression layer to predict the normalization constant Z_h dependent on h, instead of treating it as a constant.

nodes.name: perplexity
nodes.statement: We take perplexity as the performance measurement of a language model, which is defined by \[ PPL = 2^-frac1Nsum_i=1^Nlog_2 p(w_i|h_i) \] where N is the number of running words in the test corpus.
nodes.raw_latex:
We take perplexity as the performance measurement of a language model, which
is defined by
\[
\mathrm{PPL} = 2^{-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\log_2 p(w_i|h_i)}
\]
where $N$ is the number of running words in the test corpus.
